Since secondary causes like renal disease and adrenal tumors are unlikely, does the patient have signs of coarctation of the aorta, such as weak or absent pulses in the lower extremities or a blood pressure difference between the arms and legs? The echocardiogram confirms the narrowing distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, explaining the elevated upper body blood pressure and ruling out other causes of secondary hypertension.
